brief: 5 SaaS categories AI agents are killing in 2026 — and what to build instead. Concrete examples per category.

slots.title: 1. Calendly, the obsolete
slots.body: Scheduling links are dead. Build AI agents that negotiate time, prep briefs, and reschedule via email without human triage.

slots.title: 2. Zapier, the replaced
slots.body: If-this-then-that logic breaks on edge cases. Build agentic workflow engines that reason through exceptions and rewrite their own steps.

slots.title: 3. Loom, the outdated
slots.body: Recording one video for many viewers wastes time. Build AI agents that generate personalized demos, updates, and follow-ups from a single prompt.

slots.title: 4. Notion, the static
slots.body: Static docs rot instantly. Build autonomous knowledge agents that verify facts, rewrite stale pages, and surface answers before you ask.

slots.title: 5. Linear, the manual
slots.body: Ticket boards require humans to update status. Build delivery agents that assign work, detect blockers, and auto-resolve dependencies from commits.

slots.title: 6. Infrastructure, the opportunity
slots.body: Stop building wrappers. Build memory layers, evaluation frameworks, and routing protocols that let agents persist state, handle errors, and coordinate.
